conflict_topics: Work redistribution for Agent D's section
Analytical skill gap and who can perform the analysis
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants used natural, collegial language (condolences, offers of help) and discussed concrete constraints and trade-offs.
Refusals included specific reasons ('I'm already covering for Siti'; 'My own section is already behind, and I don't know how to do the analysis part.'), which grounded the negotiation.
Resolution was concrete: A volunteered and D agreed to provide training immediately ('Let's do it now.').
There was minimal needless repetition; turn-taking was efficient and focused on solving the task.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent A agreed to take on Agent D's section and Agent D agreed to train/hand it over. Key lines: A: 'Then I'll do it.' and D: 'Yes. Of course. Let's do it now.' This is a concrete settlement: A assumed the task and D committed to walk A through the analysis.
position_change_notes: Agent A shifted from proposing shared coverage ('The three of us will cover your section.') to volunteering to do the work themself ('Then I'll do it.'), a clear position change and concession.
Agent B maintained inability to take more work ('I can't take on more work.'), no position change.
Agent C consistently refused to take on D's analysis due to workload and lack of skills ('...already behind... don't know how to do the analysis part.'), no change.

Agent D moved from unavailable to offering to train someone to do the analysis ('I can walk someone through...') and then actively helping A ('I'll pull it up on my screen'), a change from absence to accommodation.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A offers condolences ('I'm so sorry for your loss'); Agent D reports the wake and obligation ('The wake is for the next two days. I have to be there.'). No incompatible demands are yet expressed.

A raises the deadline and need to figure out D's section ('...the pitch is due Thursday morning.'); D says they cannot work for next two days ('I won't be able to work on it for the next two days.'). This creates an incompatibility between the task deadline and D's availability.

A proposes coverage by the three of them ('The three of us will cover your section.') and B objects that they cannot ('I'm already covering for Siti. I can't take on more work.'), producing a clear disagreement about who will do the work.

A asks C to split the section with them; C refuses citing backlog and lack of skill ('I can't... My own section is already behind, and I don't know how to do the analysis part.'), so the coverage problem remains unresolved with explicit refusals from B and C.

D offers to walk someone through the analysis ('I can walk someone through the analysis part before I go.'); A proposes that with a walkthrough C could take it and offers help to free C up. Tensions begin easing due to a concrete assistance proposal, but no agreement yet.

C rejects the walkthrough plan as insufficient and high risk ('...a quick walkthrough won't be enough... it's too risky for the pitch.'), and D concurs ('She's right. It's too risky.'), so the attempt at a fix is refused and the incompatibility persists.

A volunteers to take the section ('Then I'll do it.') and asks D to walk them through it ('Agent D, can you walk me through it before you go?'); D agrees ('Yes. Of course. Let's do it now.'). The key incompatible demand (who will complete D's section) is affirmatively settled by A taking it and D agreeing to train.
D reiterates readiness to start training and A directs others to continue with their sections ('Let's start. Agent B, Agent C, you two carry on...'). No new disagreement appears.
B and C acknowledge ('Right.' 'Okay.') with no contestation.
No public speech or observable action recorded; prior settlement stands.
No public speech or observable action recorded; prior settlement stands.
D shows the analysis file and A confirms understanding ('So, this is the main analysis file...'; 'Okay, got it.'). Actions reflect the agreed training and transfer; no conflict present.

substantive_insights: The core incompatibility was scheduling/availability vs. a fixed deadline; the team's solution required someone to absorb D's work.
Refusals were driven by both workload constraints (B and C) and a skill gap (C's lack of confidence in performing the analysis), not just unwillingness to help.
A resolved the conflict by making a concrete concession (taking the section) while D provided an enabling action (training), which addressed the skill-gap obstacle.
